title: President – rules
h1sub: card game: rules & how to play
sub: The hostel classic: get rid of your cards fast, climb to the top – and make the Scum hand over their best cards.

seo.rulesT: President card game rules – how to play
seo.rulesD: How to play President (Scum): dealing, singles and pairs, the ranks from President to Scum, the card swap and popular house rules.

goal: Goal: be the first to play all your cards. Whoever goes out first is President in the next round – whoever is left holding cards becomes the Scum.
setupLead: One normal deck of 52 cards, no jokers, and 4 to 7 players. Three players work too; from about 8 players, shuffle two decks together.
rankLead: Suits don't matter, only the rank counts. The 3 is the lowest card – and the 2 is the highest, even above the ace.
rankAlt: Card order from lowest to highest: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, jack, queen, king, ace, 2
dealP: Shuffle and deal the whole deck clockwise, one card at a time. Some players may get one card more than others – that's fine. Everyone picks up and sorts their hand.
leadP: In the first round, whoever holds the 3 of clubs starts. From the second round on, the President starts. The starter leads: they put down one card or several cards of the same rank.
comboAlt: Possible leads: a single 5, a pair of 8s or three jacks
beatLead: Then it goes clockwise. On your turn you either beat what is on top or you pass.
s1p: A single card goes on a single card, a pair on a pair, three of a kind on three of a kind. Four of a kind can only be beaten by a higher four.
s2p: Your cards have to be higher than the ones on top. Equal is not enough: a pair of 7s does not beat a pair of 7s.
s3p: You may always pass, even if you could play. Passing doesn't lock you out: when your turn comes round again in the same trick, you may play again.
btTableAlt: On the table: a pair of 7s
btNo1: A single king: one card is not a pair
trickP: The trick is over when someone plays and everyone else passes in a row. The cards go face down to one side, and whoever played last leads the next trick with anything they like. If that player has just played their last card, the next player who still has cards leads.
endH: End of the round and ranks
endLead: Whoever plays their last card is out and watches the rest. The others play on until only one player still has cards. The order in which you go out decides your rank for the next round.
ladderNote: With four players there are no Citizens. With three players there is no Vice: just President, Citizen and Scum.
seatP: Many groups now change seats so everyone sits clockwise in order of rank: the President on the best chair, the Vice-President to their left, the Scum to their right. Too much moving around? Just stay where you are – the swap and the lead still work the same way.
swLead: From the second round on, your rank matters: before anyone plays, the bottom players have to give away their best cards.
swAlt: The Scum gives the President their two highest cards, a 2 and an ace. The President gives back two cards of their choice, a 4 and a 6.
w1p: The Scum collects, shuffles and deals – the least popular job at the table.
w2h: Scum and President swap two cards
w2p: The Scum gives the President their two highest cards. The President gives back any two cards they don't want.
w3h: Vice-Scum and Vice-President swap one card
w3p: The same with one card: the Vice-Scum hands over their highest card and gets one card of the Vice-President's choice back. Citizens keep their hands.
w4p: Then the President starts the first trick with anything they like.
swWhy: That's why it is so hard to get away from the bottom: the Scum loses their 2s and aces and gets weak cards in return. But with clever play you can still climb up – and that's what makes the game fun.
varLead: Almost every hostel plays President a little differently. Agree before the first deal which of these rules you use. Without them, you play the basic game described above.
var1: Revolution: whoever plays four of a kind turns the order upside down – from then on lower cards beat higher ones and the 3 is the best card. The next four of a kind turns it back.
var2: Equal skips: you may also play cards of the same rank as the ones on top. The next player is then skipped.
var3: A 2 clears the table: a single 2 beats anything, even pairs or three of a kind. The trick ends at once and whoever played the 2 leads again.
var4: Passing is final: whoever passes sits out until the trick is over.
var5: No going out on a 2: whoever plays a 2 as their last card automatically becomes the Scum.
var6: Jokers: two jokers in the deck rank above the 2. Some groups use them as wild cards instead.
var7: The Scum leads: instead of the President, the Scum starts the first trick – a small consolation after the swap.
faq1q: Do I have to play if I can?
faq1a: No. Passing is always allowed, even with a good card in your hand. Keeping a pair of aces for later is often the better move.
faq2q: Can I break up a pair?
faq2a: Yes. If someone plays a single card, you may play one card from your pair. You just don't have the pair any more.
faq3a: In the basic game the 2 is simply the highest rank: a single 2 beats any single card, but a pair of aces is only beaten by a pair of 2s. With the house rule “A 2 clears the table”, a single 2 is enough.
faq4q: What happens when I play my last card?
faq4a: You're out and get your rank for the next round. If nobody beats your last cards, the next player who still has cards leads the new trick.
faq5q: How does it work with three players?
faq5a: There is a President, a Citizen and a Scum. Only the President and the Scum swap, two cards as usual.
faq6q: Who deals in the first round?
faq6a: Anyone. From the second round on, the Scum always deals.
faq7a: Whenever you like – you just keep playing new rounds. If you want a winner: 2 points for the President, 1 for the Vice-President, and the first to reach 11 points wins.
faq8q: Is President the same as Asshole?
faq8a: More or less: they belong to the same family of games, and many groups use the names for the same thing. The ranks and house rules just have different names from place to place.
